title: sieve-native: lexer and recursive-descent parser
description:
Implement the tokenizer and a generic form reader. The parser has zero knowledge of Sieve commands or grammar — it just reads forms.

What: src/lexer.rs + src/form.rs

Core insight: Sieve syntax is a Lisp-family form language. Every statement is:
  command :tag arg :tag arg test_or_testlist block?
which maps directly to a flat Vec<Form>. No grammar rules needed in the parser.

Form type (form.rs):
  pub enum Form {
      Word(String),               // bare word — command name or extension name
      Tag(String),                // :contains, :over, :is etc  (colon stripped)
      Str(String),                // "quoted string"
      Num(u64),                   // integer literal
      StringList(Vec<String>),    // ["a", "b", "c"]
      TestList(Vec<Stmt>),        // (test, test, test)  — allof/anyof args
      Block(Vec<Stmt>),           // { stmt; stmt; }
  }
  pub type Stmt = Vec<Form>;      // first element is always Word(command)
  pub type Script = Vec<Stmt>;

Lexer (lexer.rs) — tokens only, no Sieve knowledge:
  pub enum Token { Word(String), Tag(String), StringLit(String), Number(u64),
                   LBracket, RBracket, LParen, RParen, LBrace, RBrace, Semicolon, Comma }
  pub fn tokenize(src: &str) -> Result<Vec<Token>, ParseError>
  Handle: quoted strings with \-escapes, multi-line strings (text: ... .CRLF), # comments, numbers.
  ParseError carries line+column.

Form reader (form.rs):
  pub fn read_script(tokens: &[Token]) -> Result<Script, ParseError>
  Algorithm:
  1. read_stmt(): consume tokens up to Semicolon or LBrace; collect as Vec<Form>.
     Each token maps to exactly one Form variant.
     LBracket → read_string_list() → StringList.
     LParen   → read_test_list()  → TestList  (comma-separated stmts, no semicolons).
     LBrace   → read_block()      → Block     (recursive read_script() until RBrace).
  2. read_script() = loop calling read_stmt() until tokens exhausted.

The form reader is ~80 lines. It knows about brackets, parens, braces, and semicolons. Nothing else.

Defensive rules:
  - Unclosed bracket/brace/paren → ParseError with position.
  - Empty StringList is valid ([]).
  - Non-string tokens inside StringList → ParseError (strings only in [...]).
  - No unwrap(); all token exhaustion → ParseError.
